> **Key Takeaways**
>
>
> • CombineHealth is an AI-powered revenue cycle platform for orthopedics that learns from every denial, reimbursement, and underpayment to adapt billing strategy for each payer. Its orthopedic coding covers laterality, fracture specificity, modifiers, NCCI bundling logic, and global-period scenarios. It manages each case through eligibility, pre-bill validation, claims, denials, A/R follow-up, and appeals, reporting up to 85% automation and up to 75% fewer coding-related denials.
>
>
> • A good orthopedic medical billing service closes revenue leaks at the source. Common leaks include modifier 25 on a same-day injection, an implant invoice that never reaches the payer, and a laterality gap in an operative note. Vendors do this through AI that codes and validates every encounter, specialist billing teams that take over the department, or a combination, and each model fits a different practice.
>
>
> • Orthopedic billing vendors charge a percentage of collections, a flat monthly fee, a per-claim fee, or a software subscription. Compare net cost against the denial rate and collection rate each vendor commits to, not the fee alone.
>
>
> • Outsource orthopedic billing when turnover, denial backlogs, or surgical volume outpace your billing office. Keep it in-house when your team has orthopedic coding depth. Hybrid models add AI coding or audits to an in-house team.
>
>
> • Orthopedic claims are commonly denied for five reasons: modifier errors on 25 and 59, NCCI bundling edits, global period conflicts, missing prior authorization, and operative notes that omit laterality or implant details.
>
>
> • A global period bundles routine post-operative care into the surgical fee. Major surgeries typically carry 90 days under Medicare. Modifier 24 covers an unrelated visit during that period, and modifier 79 covers an unrelated procedure.
>
>
> • AI can code orthopedic surgical cases accurately when it reads the full operative note and applies payer requirements. An audit mode lets it review codes produced by surgeons, coders, or existing billing companies, so a practice can adopt it without replacing its current workflow.


A single total knee replacement sets off a long chain of billing decisions before the claim ever leaves the building. The surgeon documents the approach, the implant, the side, and what was found in the joint. A coder then converts that note into Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) and[ICD-10-CM codes](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/icd-10-explained-a-comprehensive-guide-to-medical-coding) , applies modifiers, checks bundling edits, and tracks a 90-day global period that decides which follow-up visits are payable. One missing detail returns the claim weeks later as a denial.


Anyone who has run an orthopedic revenue cycle knows where the money leaks. The money leaves through modifier 25 on a same-day injection, an implant invoice that never reaches the payer, or a laterality gap in an operative note that nobody caught before submission. Each leak looks small until a month of them lands on the[accounts receivable (A/R) report](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ar-follow-up-software-medical-billing) .


The right orthopedic medical billing service closes those leaks at the source. Some vendors do it with AI that codes and validates every encounter. Others assign specialist billing teams to take over the department, and a few combine both. Each model fits a different practice, and choosing the wrong one costs months.


This guide compares ten vendors that publicly document both orthopedic coding and orthopedic billing capabilities.

## 1. CombineHealth: AI-Powered Orthopedic Medical Billing


[CombineHealth](https://www.combinehealth.ai/) is an AI-powered revenue cycle platform for orthopedic practices, multisurgeon groups, ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs), hospitals, management services organizations (MSOs), and billing organizations. Self-learning autonomous medical coding sits at the core of the entire workflow. Every claim outcome returns to the coding engine to refine the next decision.


Also referred to as[Amy AI](https://www.combinehealth.ai/ai-medical-coding-software) , the CombineHealth medical coding platform reads completed encounter documentation directly from the electronic health record (EHR) and carries each case through eligibility, pre-bill validation, claims, denials, A/R follow-up, and appeals. Its orthopedic offering is built around[procedure-specific CPT](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/orthopedic-cpt-codes) and ICD requirements, surgical rules, ASC-versus-hospital differences, and payer requirements.


CombineHealth’s edge in[orthopedic medical billing](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/orthopedic-cpt-codes) is payer intelligence. The platform learns from every denial, reimbursement, and underpayment, and it adapts billing strategy for each payer. That matters in a specialty where payers apply their own bundling edits, modifier 25 and 59 scrutiny, global period policies, implant carve-out rules, and prior authorization requirements to the same procedure.


### **Feature #1: Billing-Ready Orthopedic Code Generation**


CombineHealth assigns[evaluation and management (E/M) levels](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/e-m-coding-guide) , CPT procedure codes,[ICD-10-CM](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/icd-10-codes-for-orthopedic-surgery) diagnosis codes, Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Level II codes,[modifiers](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/modifiers-in-medical-billing) , and diagnosis sequencing from the completed operative note. It captures laterality, anatomical and fracture specificity, and CPT-to-diagnosis linkage, with automation rates of up to 85%.


### **Feature #2: Payer Intelligence**


CombineHealth[tracks denials](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/denial-management-in-healthcare) , reimbursements, and[underpayments](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/healthcare-underpayments-guide) by payer and adapts coding strategy accordingly, with up to a 75% reduction in coding-related denials.


### **Feature #3: Explainability in Medical Coding**


Every code links to the supporting documentation, coding rationale, applicable guidance, and payer requirements, which gives coders, auditors, and compliance teams a complete[audit trail](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-audit-trail-work-for-medical-coding) .


### **Feature #4: Surgical Rules, Bundling, and Global-Period Logic**


CombineHealth applies modifiers, National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) bundling logic, and global-period scenarios, and it accounts for ASC-versus-hospital differences in orthopedic coding.


### **Feature #5: Documentation Gap Detection**


CombineHealth flags missing laterality, fracture details, operative information, medical-necessity support, and modifier evidence. Clinical documentation improvement ([CDI](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/clinical-documentation-improvement-guide) ) alerts and physician queries reach surgeons before the claim goes out.


### **Feature #6: Autonomous and Audit Modes**


CombineHealth codes eligible encounters autonomously, or audits codes produced by surgeons, coders, EHRs, existing billing companies, and other coding platforms.


### **Feature #7: Billing and RCM Workflows**


CombineHealth verifies eligibility and benefits, checks authorization requirements, validates claims before submission, classifies denials, drafts appeals, follows up on A/R, and analyzes underpayments.


**Best For:** Orthopedic practices, multisurgeon groups, ASCs, hospital-employed groups, MSOs, and billing organizations that want to automate coding, billing checks, denials, and appeals end-to-end, with explainable decisions they can defend in an audit.


## 2. Maia: AI Coding & Billing Software for Orthopedic Practices


Maia is an AI-powered medical coding and RCM software platform built specifically for orthopaedic practices. Its AutoCoder product targets E/M coding, surgical coding, denial appeals, and prior authorizations, and it shows a justification for every code it selects. Maia announced a $1.2 million seed round on June 16, 2026, and its roadmap adds prior authorization, denial appeal automation, AI documentation support, and an AI scribe. As an early-stage software vendor, Maia gives practices a specialty-only coding & billing layer that their own teams operate.


**Key Features:**


- E/M and surgical coding for orthopedic encounters
- Code-level justification for every selection
- Fine-tuned medical language models combined with clinical rules and expert feedback
- Denial appeal and prior authorization support
- Clinical advisory board of orthopaedic surgeons
- Roadmap for AI documentation support and an AI scribe


**Best For:** Orthopedic groups that want a specialty-only AI coding & billing product they operate in-house.

A 2024 partnership with HST Pathways connects ASC software to its services. A 2026 ROI validation report states that Compass Surgical Partners onboarded six pilot ASCs in four weeks and lowered cost to collect from 3% to 2.5% of net revenue.

- End-to-end managed RCM for orthopedic and musculoskeletal practices
- AAOE Peer Review designation
- ASC and facility billing support through the HST Pathways integration
- Technology-enabled workflows
- Documented ASC onboarding speed and cost-to-collect results


**Best For:** Orthopedic groups and ASC operators that want a fully outsourced revenue cycle with a peer-validated partner.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Orthopedic Medical Billing Services


### How does CombineHealth reduce orthopedic coding denials?


CombineHealth learns from every denial, reimbursement, and underpayment and adapts billing strategy for each payer — payer intelligence, not static rules. That matters in orthopedics, where payers apply their own bundling edits, modifier 25 and 59 scrutiny, global-period policies, and implant carve-out rules to the same procedure. The approach has been tied to up to a 75% reduction in coding-related denials, and every code carries a rationale that speeds appeals on the denials that remain.


### Does CombineHealth capture laterality, fracture detail, and implants from the operative note?


Yes. CombineHealth reads the completed operative note and captures laterality, anatomical and fracture specificity, and CPT-to-diagnosis linkage, and it accounts for implant and device rules including invoice-based carve-outs. Where the note is missing laterality, fracture details, operative information, or implant evidence, it flags the gap and sends a CDI query to the surgeon before the claim goes out — closing the exact leaks that return orthopedic claims as denials.


### Does CombineHealth handle the full orthopedic revenue cycle or just coding?


The full cycle. Self-learning autonomous coding sits at the core, but CombineHealth also verifies eligibility and benefits, checks authorization requirements, validates claims before submission, classifies denials, drafts appeals, follows up on A/R, and analyzes underpayments — all on one platform, so coding decisions and downstream payer outcomes inform one another.


### Can CombineHealth audit codes our current orthopedic billing company or coders produce?


Yes. In audit mode, CombineHealth independently evaluates codes produced by surgeons, coders, EHRs, existing billing companies, or other coding platforms against the full documentation, flagging discrepancies with the supporting evidence and rationale shown. Practices often start here to validate current coding and quantify leakage before expanding to autonomous coding.


### How Do Global Periods Affect Orthopedic Billing?


A global period bundles routine post-operative care into the surgical fee. Major surgeries typically carry 90 days under Medicare. Modifier 24 covers an unrelated visit, and modifier 79 covers an unrelated procedure.


### Can AI Code Orthopedic Surgical Cases Accurately?


AI can code orthopedic surgical cases accurately when it reads the full operative note and applies payer requirements. CombineHealth reports up to 85% automation, and its audit mode reviews codes from surgeons, coders, or existing billing companies.
